policy_title: Accelerate Environmental Land Management Schemes with Extra Funding
stated: Accelerate the rollout of the new Environmental Land Management schemes, properly funding it with an extra £1 billion a year to support profitable, sustainable and nature-friendly farming.

source.quote: Accelerate the rollout of the new Environmental Land Management schemes, properly funding it with an extra £1 billion a year to support profitable, sustainable and nature-friendly farming.

bearing_set.reason: ELM schemes directly pay farmers for environmental public goods — biodiversity, clean water, carbon sequestration, soil health — so extra funding and accelerated rollout has a material, non-negligible effect on emissions trajectory, water quality, and nature.

The policy explicitly targets 'profitable' farming; an extra £1bn channelled through ELM directly affects farm incomes and the economic viability of agricultural livelihoods, earning a real verdict on whether farming constitutes decent, secure work.

The policy explicitly targets 'profitable, sustainable' farming; how ELM funding affects farm incomes, agricultural productivity and the viability of the rural economy during the CAP-to-ELM transition is a genuine and contested prosperity question.
An extra £1 billion per year is a material additional spending commitment; whether it is funded or borrowed directly affects the debt-path and fiscal sustainability indicators.

membership_note: Core bearing is environmental (O6), with a real prosperity question for the agricultural sector (O13) and a concrete fiscal commitment that must route to O12. Effects on food prices (O2) and farm-worker pay (O4) are too indirect and marginal to clear the non-negligible bar.
